entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *obtuse*: formal reproach - slow to understand, and perhaps unwilling to.
examples: he had so rapaciously desired and so obtusely expected to find her alone

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Also a charge - *disorderly conduct* - which lends the ordinary sense weight.

entries.definition: worn from age or heavy use and no longer able to operate (of cars or machines or people)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British, and it works equally on a car, a machine or a person - which is the joke.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The sound of the word carries the speed; brisk contempt rather than anger.

entries.definition: given to haughty disregard of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: About a single act more often than a character - a decision taken over someone's head.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Of a thing rather than a person - honest money, honest weight; it lends objects a moral character.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gentle and slightly religious - death as a journey rather than an end.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The commoner form, and now used almost exclusively as an accusation.
examples: she was anything but puritanical in her behavior

entries.definition: noisy like the sound of a bee
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same sound, and equally likely to describe excitement as annoyance.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *blithe*: splits sharply: blithe spirits are charming, *blithe disregard* is careless.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elevated and old; the boasting is grand enough to sound almost heroic.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *dour*: unyielding and unsmiling; it judges the manner as much as the will.
examples: he sat in his chair dourly

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cruel*: the central moral charge: the suffering was known about and inflicted anyway.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely procedural; the word belongs to committees.
examples: the mother was stern and disciplinary

entries.definition: concerned chiefly or only with yourself and your advantage to the exclusion of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain moral word, and the one that gets used in real arguments.
examples: Selfish men were … trying to make capital for themselves out of the sacred cause of civil rights

entries.definition: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Religious in origin; it condemns the thing as unfit rather than merely dirty.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Big, loud and unrestrained - hearty rather than refined.

entries.definition: humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gentleness of manner with no claim about the will behind it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gravestone language - comfort offered to the living.

entries.definition: possessing or displaying courage; able to face and deal with danger or fear without flinching
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain, universal praise - facing what frightens you.
examples: Familiarity with danger makes a brave man braver but less daring
a brave decision to speak up

entries.definition: feeling pleasurable satisfaction over something by which you measures your self-worth
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Quiet satisfaction in something you did - modest and unobjectionable.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *lifeless*: clinical and detached - describes a body, not a person.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise with a shrug - big of you can be sincere or sarcastic, and often is.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *grudging*: the money was given - resentfully, which is what makes it worse than refusal for some.
examples: he grudgingly agreed to have a drink in a hotel close by

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *brutal*: plain and physical. The commonest of the strong words, and the least ornamented.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sincerity that shows its effort, which is why it can be faintly comic.

entries.definition: ill-mannered and coarse and contemptible in behavior or appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Young, male and physical - the lout takes up space and does not apologise.
examples: the loutish manners of a bully

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *gluttonous*: names one of the seven deadly sins; the excess is a moral failure, not an appetite.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Praise with a purpose; the compliment is a means, and both parties usually know it.

entries.definition: marked by or showing unaffected simplicity and lack of guile or worldly experience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The French spelling, used when the writer wants a touch of distance.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling, identical in force.

entries.definition: express complaints, discontent, displeasure, or unhappiness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The complaint is unasked-for and delivered at length.

entries.definition: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cuts twice - shallow work, and often a shallow person implied behind it.
examples: In his paper, he showed a very superficial understanding of psychoanalytic theory

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - crying treated as whining, weakness rather than sorrow.
examples: Stop snivelling — you got yourself into this mess!

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The common form, and the one that still gets used in earnest.
examples: gave wholehearted support to her candidacy

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cleverness that sparkles in company.
examples: a play full of scintillating dialogue

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Thoroughly bad, with a hint of moral distaste.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *dingy*: said of rooms and fabric, and the real complaint is that it is depressing.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *sloppy*: the everyday version, mild enough to say to someone's face.
examples: this work was done rather sloppily

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Church Latin behind it; it lifts the praise onto a ceremonial register.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries a trace of prayer - thanks owed to providence as much as to a person.

entries.definition: in an offensive and hateful manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *repulsive*: ugliness that actively drives people away.

entries.definition: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Compares the eater to a pig outright, with none of the softening *piggy* has.

entries.definition: with pride; in a proud manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The adverb of *proud*: genuinely two-faced: proud of your children is warm, proud to a fault is a failing. Context decides.

entries.definition: marked by barbarity suggestive of a cannibal; rapaciously savage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The furthest word in the family, and rare enough to sound like an accusation of myth.

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Softer and older than *kind*, and now used mostly of the elderly.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Withering - stupidity so complete it deserves contempt.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *trim*: neat and in good shape - credits effort.

entries.definition: having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Wealth as a class marker, often said with a raised eyebrow.

entries.definition: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the betrayal of someone who trusted you - the harm is to a relationship, not to the truth.
